newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty attacks Palestinians over human rights.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty attacks Palestinians over human rights.

text.p: Amnesty International on Monday criticised what it called a worrying increase in human rights abuses by the Palestinian Authority over the past two years.
The London-based human rights organisation said this had been coupled with an emerging climate of fear and intimidation in areas under the Authority's jurisdiction.
"Victims of brutal torture and other abuses are now afraid to speak out and give their names in the face of threats," Amnesty said in a statement.
"This is a fearsome indictment of a system which ignores the people who complain of abuse and threatens them with reprisals," it added.

Amnesty said in a report there was a "growing climate of fear" in Palestinian areas, where journalists who reported abuses were arrested, their newspapers closed down and prominent human rights activists harassed.
Over the past two years Amnesty International delegates including medical personnel had visited the Palestinian Authority several times.
Amnesty said it had documented human rights abuses committed by the 10 or so Palestinian security services in the areas under the Palestinian Authority's jurisdiction.

These included the "arbitrary political arrest and prolonged detention without charge or trial of hundreds of suspected political opponents, widespread use of torture and unlawful killings, the failure to adequately investigate abuses and the arrest of journalists and human rights defenders who denounce them".

Amnesty said mass detentions of suspected opponents of the peace process had been carried out following pressure by Israel and the United States to clamp down on those responsible for violent attacks on Israeli citizens.

The Palestinian Authority should use internationally recognised standards to bring to justice those who had committed violent acts and there was no justification for the use of torture and other serious human rights abuses, said Amnesty.
It said at least nine people had died in the custody of the Palestinian security services in circumstances where torture appeared to have caused or contributed to their deaths.

The legal system had been "marginalised and ignored" as political detainees were held with no reference to any law. Few of those arrested made any attempt to hire a lawyer as "they know it will make no difference", Amnesty said.
